dedupe_keys.name: map of built up expansion nedbygging over norway 2017 2022 version 2

description: This dataset maps polygons of potential built-up expansion (nedbygging), where natural land was converted to built-up surfaces such as buildings and roads, across mainland Norway between 2017 and 2022. It was produced by Zander Venter of the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research (NINA) with NRK journalists Mads Nyborg Støstad, Ruben Solvang, Anne Linn Kumano-Ensby and Su Thet Mon for an NRK article of 6 January 2024; version 2 was published on Zenodo on 27 June 2024. Polygons come from Sentinel-2 imagery, Google's Dynamic World land cover model and NINA's time-series analysis, joined by NRK where they belong to one event. Version 2 adds crowdsourced verification labels from an interactive app, the year of change and NRK's type labels; attributes record whether a polygon was checked against orthophotos and whether the AI was right. Coverage: mainland Norway, excluding Svalbard. Access: a shapefile of about 13 MB on Zenodo and an Earth Engine viewer. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: the false positive rate was 18 per cent on 500 validation points, and small cabins and forestry roads are often missed. Simulation uses: tracking urban and cabin growth, land take and exposure of new development. Related records: the Germany building types map and GlobalBuildingAtlas.
name: Map of built-up expansion (nedbygging) over Norway 2017-2022, version 2
